nodes.label: Rainwater Harvesting
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Traditional systems: Rajasthan (khadins, johads, tankas), Maharashtra (bandharas, phads), MP (bundelas - chanderis), Bihar (ahars, pynes), Tamil Nadu rooftop harvesting mandatory. Modern revival of traditional systems.

nodes.label: Bhakra Nangal Dam
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: On Sutlej river in Himachal Pradesh/Punjab border. One of highest gravity dams in world (226m). Govind Sagar reservoir. Provides irrigation and hydropower to Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan.

nodes.label: Water Scarcity
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Growing due to over-exploitation, excessive use in agriculture and industry, unequal access. Climate change affecting rainfall patterns. Groundwater depletion in Punjab, Haryana, western UP. Quality deterioration from pollution.

nodes.label: IT and Electronics Industry
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Fastest growing industry. Bengaluru electronics capital of India. Other centres: Mumbai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Pune, Chennai, Kolkata, Lucknow. Major exports: software services. 31% of global IT exports from India.

nodes.label: Industrial Pollution
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Air pollution from smoke, gases, chemicals. Water pollution from effluents (organic/inorganic, toxic). Soil and noise pollution. Thermal pollution from power plants. Need for NAAQS, ZED certification, effluent treatment.

nodes.label: Indian Ports
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: 13 major and 200+ minor/intermediate ports. 95% of trade by volume through ports. Major ports: Mumbai, JNPT (Nhava Sheva), Kandla, Kochi, Chennai, Visakhapatnam, Kolkata-Haldia, Paradip, Marmagao, New Mangalore, Tuticorin, Ennore.

nodes.label: Richter Scale
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Logarithmic scale measuring earthquake magnitude based on amplitude of seismic waves. Each whole number increase represents 10x increase in amplitude and approximately 31.6x increase in energy. Developed by Charles Richter in 1935. Scale is open-ended but earthquakes above 9.0 are extremely rare.

nodes.label: National Park
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Strictly protected area for conservation of wildlife and natural habitats. No human activities like grazing, forestry, or cultivation allowed. Boundaries fixed by legislation. India has 106 national parks covering about 1.35% of the country. Notable: Jim Corbett (first, 1936), Kaziranga, Ranthambore, Sundarbans, Gir.

nodes.label: India's Coastline
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: India has a total coastline of about 7,516.6 km. Mainland coastline is about 6,100 km. Two coastlines: Western coast (Arabian Sea) and Eastern coast (Bay of Bengal). 9 coastal states and 4 Union Territories. Longest coastline: Gujarat. Important ports on both coasts. EEZ extends 200 nautical miles from coast.

nodes.label: Arabian Sea
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Northwestern part of the Indian Ocean between India and the Arabian Peninsula. India's western coastline faces the Arabian Sea. Major ports: Mumbai, Kandla, Cochin, Mormugao. Lakshadweep Islands located here. Arabian Sea branch of monsoon brings heavy rainfall to Western Ghats. Important for trade routes to Middle East and Europe.

nodes.label: Bay of Bengal
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Northeastern part of the Indian Ocean between India, Bangladesh, Myanmar, and Sri Lanka. World's largest bay. India's eastern coastline faces it. Andaman and Nicobar Islands located here. Bay of Bengal branch of monsoon brings rainfall to eastern India. Prone to tropical cyclones. Receives drainage of Ganga, Brahmaputra, and other major rivers.

nodes.label: Kanyakumari
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Southernmost point of the Indian mainland at about 8d4'N. Located in Tamil Nadu where the Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal, and Indian Ocean meet. Tip of the Indian peninsula. Not the southernmost point of India (which is Indira Point on Great Nicobar). Historical and cultural significance.

nodes.label: Phases of Population Growth in India
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Four phases: Phase I (1901-1921) stagnant growth; Phase II (1921-1951) steady growth; Phase III (1951-1981) population explosion; Phase IV (post-1981) declining growth rate. 1921 is called the demographic divide.
nodes.chapter_title: Population: Distribution, Density, Growth and Composition

nodes.label: Urbanisation in India
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Urban growth accelerated since 1931 due to economic development and improved health. Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Bangalore attract migrants due to industrial development. Rural-urban migration conspicuous along road and rail links.
nodes.chapter_title: Population: Distribution, Density, Growth and Composition

nodes.label: Life-time Migrant
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Person whose place of birth differs from place of enumeration. Census records migration since 1881. 307 million life-time migrants recorded in Census 2001.

nodes.label: Industrial Regions
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Mumbai-Pune, Bangalore-Chennai, Hugli, Ahmedabad-Vadodara, Chotanagpur, Delhi-Meerut. Concentration where factors converge.

nodes.label: Swadeshi and Textile
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Boycott of British goods gave impetus. After 1921, railway enabled Coimbatore, Madurai, Nagpur, Indore centres.

nodes.label: Pipelines
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: First: Naharkatiya-Barauni 1,157 km. HVJ pipeline. Salaya-Mathura 1,256 km. OIL manages.

nodes.label: Airports
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: 12 international: Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata, Bangalore, Hyderabad. 112 domestic. High-value perishable goods.

nodes.label: Nomadic Herding
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Primitive subsistence. Three regions: N.Africa-Arabia-Mongolia; Tundra; SW Africa. Transhumance seasonal vertical movement. Declining.

nodes.label: Commercial Livestock
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Organised, capital intensive, permanent ranches. Scientific breeding. NZ, Australia, Argentina, Uruguay, USA.

nodes.label: Shifting Cultivation
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Slash and burn. 3-5 years then abandoned. Jhuming (NE India), Milpa (C.America), Ladang (Indonesia). Cycle shortening.

nodes.label: Intensive Subsistence
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Monsoon Asia. Wet paddy (small holdings, manual, high yield/area) and non-paddy (wheat N.China, millets dry India).

nodes.label: Plantation Agriculture
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: European colonies. Large estates, capital intensive, single crop, cheap labour, export. Tea/rubber/coffee/sugarcane.

nodes.label: Dairy Farming
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Most advanced milch rearing. Capital/labour intensive. Near urban centres. NW Europe, Canada, SE Australia/NZ.

nodes.label: Mediterranean Agriculture
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Specialised commercial. Citrus, viticulture (grapes/wine), olives. Mediterranean shores, S.California, Chile.

nodes.label: Cooperative/Collective Farming
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Cooperative: voluntary (Denmark). Collective/Kolkhoz: social ownership (Soviet). State controls production.

nodes.label: Sahara Desert
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: World's largest hot desert in North Africa, area about 8.54 million sq km. Touches eleven countries. Besides sand, has gravel plains and elevated rocky plateaus over 2500m. Al Azizia recorded highest temp 57.7C (1922).

nodes.label: Sahara Climate
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Scorching hot and dry. Short rainy season. Cloudless clear sky. Day temperatures soar to 50C heating sand and rocks. Nights freezing cold near zero. Moisture evaporates faster than accumulates.

nodes.label: Oasis
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Green islands in desert where underground water reaches surface in depressions formed by wind. Fertile areas where people settle, grow date palms and crops. Tafilalet Oasis in Morocco is about 13,000 sq km.

nodes.label: Bedouins and Tuaregs
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Nomadic tribes of Sahara rearing goats, sheep, camels, horses. Animals provide milk, leather, hair for mats and carpets. Wear heavy robes against dust storms and hot winds. Tuaregs now act as tourist guides.

nodes.label: Sahara Oil Discovery
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Oil discovered in Algeria, Libya, Egypt. Other minerals: iron, phosphorus, manganese, uranium. Transforming the cultural landscape with modern buildings and superhighways replacing camel paths.

nodes.label: Hot Desert
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Characterized by scorching heat during day, cold nights, scanty rainfall, sparse vegetation. Located in tropical western margins of continents. Examples: Sahara, Thar, Arabian.

nodes.label: Water Conservation
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Rain water harvesting, lining canals, sprinkler irrigation, drip irrigation. Treating effluents before discharge. Forest cover slows runoff and replenishes groundwater. One rain spell of 2 hours saves 8000 litres.
nodes.chapter_title: Land, Soil, Water, Natural Vegetation and Wildlife Resources

nodes.label: Soil Conservation Methods
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Mulching (organic cover retains moisture), contour barriers, rock dams (slow water), terrace farming (flat steps on slopes), intercropping (alternate row crops), contour ploughing, shelter belts (tree rows in coastal/dry areas).
nodes.chapter_title: Land, Soil, Water, Natural Vegetation and Wildlife Resources

nodes.label: Nuclear Power
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: From fission of uranium and thorium atoms. Greatest producers: USA, Europe. India: uranium in Rajasthan, Jharkhand; thorium in monazite sands of Kerala. Plants at Kalpakkam, Tarapur, Narora, Kaiga.

nodes.label: Subsistence Farming
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Practised to meet farmer's family needs. Low technology, household labour, small output. Includes intensive subsistence (small plots, more labour, rice main crop, monsoon Asia) and primitive subsistence (shifting cultivation, nomadic herding).

nodes.label: Commercial Farming
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Crops grown and animals reared for sale. Large area, capital and machinery. Includes commercial grain farming (wheat, maize in temperate grasslands), mixed farming (food+fodder+livestock), plantation (single crop: tea, coffee, rubber).

nodes.label: Tea and Coffee
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Tea: beverage crop needing cool climate, distributed high rainfall, well-drained loamy soil, gentle slopes. Major: Kenya, India, China, Sri Lanka. Coffee: warm wet climate, well-drained loamy soil, hill slopes. Brazil leads, followed by Columbia, India.

nodes.label: Agro-based Industries
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Use plant and animal products as raw materials. Food processing, vegetable oil, cotton textile, dairy products, leather industries. Among the oldest industrial activities.

nodes.label: Mineral-based Industries
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Primary industries using mineral ores. Products feed other industries. Iron from iron ore used for heavy machinery, building materials, railway coaches.

nodes.label: India - Size and Extent
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Area 3.28 million sq km (2.4% of world, 7th largest). Mainland latitudes 8d4'N to 37d6'N, longitudes 68d7'E to 97d25'E. N-S 3214 km, E-W 2933 km. Tropic of Cancer divides India roughly in half.

nodes.label: Standard Meridian of India
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: 82d30'E longitude passing through Mirzapur (near Allahabad). IST is 5h30m ahead of GMT. Without it, local time difference between Arunachal and Gujarat would be about 2 hours.

nodes.label: India's Land Neighbours
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Seven countries share land borders: Pakistan, Afghanistan (through PoK), China, Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar, Bangladesh. Two island neighbours across sea: Sri Lanka and Maldives.

nodes.label: Palk Strait and Gulf of Mannar
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Palk Strait separates India from Sri Lanka. Gulf of Mannar lies between India and Sri Lanka. Together they form narrow channel between southeastern India and northeastern Sri Lanka.

nodes.label: India's Young Fold Mountains and Ancient Peninsula
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Himalayas are young fold mountains still being uplifted. Peninsular plateau is one of the oldest landmasses with ancient rocks. Contrast between young, unstable north and ancient, stable south.

nodes.label: SAARC
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation. India's central position in South Asia enables contact with neighbours. India has strong historical, cultural and trade links with Southeast Asia.

nodes.label: The Peninsular Plateau
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Tableland of old crystalline, igneous and metamorphic rocks. Two divisions: Central Highlands (north of Narmada) and Deccan Plateau (south). Narmada-Tapi trough on northern flank. Chotanagpur plateau in NE extension.

nodes.label: Indian Islands
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Andaman-Nicobar in Bay of Bengal (elongated chain, point of Andaman emergence of submarine mountains). Lakshadweep in Arabian Sea (coral atolls, 36 islands). Islands important for strategic defence and biodiversity.
